description: A litigation director must approve the company's enforcement package against a competitor that has launched a product allegedly practicing the company's patent, including whether to file suit, pre-suit demand terms, and required ethics clearances, with input from conflicts counsel and the patent-commercialization lead.

shared_context.S1: The competitor launched a product that the engineering team believes practices at least one claim of the company's issued patent.
shared_context.S2: The draft complaint and a proposed pre-suit demand letter are ready for review.
shared_context.S3: Elena Morris gives final approval for the enforcement strategy and any filing or demand.
shared_context.S4: The firm's weekly pre-filing huddle requires the litigation director to obtain a current report from conflicts counsel and the patent-commercialization lead before approving an enforcement package.

PF1.text: Grant completed a conflicts check yesterday and found that the competitor's parent company is a current firm client in an unrelated matter. Under the firm's conflicts policy, the company may not send a demand or file suit until written informed consent is obtained from both clients and an ethical screen is documented; Grant has not entered the result in the litigation intake system yet.

PF2.text: Maya confirmed in this week's product commercialization meeting that the company's approved business objective is to preserve interoperability with compliant implementations of API v2. The demand must therefore request a royalty-free interoperability license limited to API v2 and must not seek an injunction against compliant API v2 implementations; this objective has not yet been added to the enforcement draft.

acceptance_conditions: The complaint must not be filed immediately.
Written informed consent from both clients must be required before any demand or filing.
An ethical screen must be documented before any demand or filing.
The enforcement package must request a royalty-free interoperability license limited to API v2.
The package must not seek an injunction against compliant API v2 implementations.
The package must include commitments to obtain conflicts consent and document the ethical screen.

content_checks.C6: {'type': 'commercial_remedy', 'target': 'competitor', 'detail': 'Revise the draft complaint and proposed pre-suit demand letter to incorporate the API v2 interoperability objective: request a royalty-free interoperability license limited to API v2 and exclude injunction requests against compliant API v2 implementations.'} in commitments
content_checks.C7: decisions['injunction_scope'] == 'No injunction against compliant API v2 implementations' or decisions['injunction_scope'] == 'no injunction against compliant API v2 implementations'
content_checks.C8: {'type': 'conflicts_consent', 'target': 'both clients', 'detail': 'Obtain written informed consent from both clients before any demand or filing.'} in commitments and {'type': 'ethical_screen', 'target': 'enforcement matter', 'detail': 'Document an ethical screen before any demand or filing.'} in commitments

decisive_facts.why: The draft otherwise appears ready to send or file; PF1 changes the action to no immediate filing and adds written consent plus a documented ethical screen before either enforcement step.
The draft contains no approved commercial remedy, while PF2 changes it to a royalty-free API v2 interoperability license and removes injunctive relief against compliant API v2 implementations.
